newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-TWO TAX-CHEAT REFEREES RESIGN.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-TWO TAX-CHEAT REFEREES RESIGN.

text.p: Two National Basketball Association referees who pleaded guilty to felony tax charges have resigned, the league said on Friday.

Jess Kersey was given three years probation and a $20,000 fine upon pleading guilty to filing a false federal income tax return. He also agreed to cooperate with federal officials, who continue their investigation of all NBA referees.

Kersey and George Toliver are the most recent referees indicted. Mike Mathis and Hank Armstrong also are awaiting trial on similar tax charges, and a government investigation is on-going with additional prosecutions likely.
Kersey, one of the best and most respected NBA officials, began his career in 1973. He worked 14 NBA Finals and three All-Star Games in his career.

In May, Mathis was indicted by a federal grand jury in U.S. District Court in Cincinnati on five counts of falsely reporting income from 1989 to 1992. The amount not reported is nearly $70,000, according to the indictment. Toliver and Armstrong were indicted in February.

According to the indictment, the four referees traded first-class airline tickets provided by the league for cheaper coach class tickets, pocketed the difference and did not report the financial gains on their federal income tax returns.
